answer: A cluster bond makes sybils expensive: every member stakes collateral that is slashed jointly when any one of them is caught faking attestations. Splitting into k clones therefore multiplies the collateral at risk instead of diluting it, because correlated faults burn the shared pool. Picture yarrow, whose many small florets ride one root system: cut a single floret and the whole head wilts. An identity may wander between clusters, yet the ferrous record of burned bonds sticks to it, so cheap throwaway personas never stay cheap.
